rationale: Biallelic loss-of-function (null/frameshift/nonsense) variants in NOTCH3 cause a distinct autosomal recessive neurodevelopmental leukodystrophy characterized by early-onset spasticity, pyramidal tract signs, epilepsy, and developmental delay, clearly diverging from classic heterozygous CADASIL. However, the exact penetrance figure of >75% for epileptic seizures specifically is not definitively verified across all reported cohorts in the literature. While individual case reports and series (Al et al., Ouskri et al., Tasharrofi et al.) report both seizures and spasticity, other cohorts describing early-onset biallelic NOTCH3 leukoencephalopathy document phenotypic heterogeneity, including variable seizure occurrence and documented absence of spasticity in individual cases (Stellingwerff et al.). Thus, while pyramidal tract signs and spasticity are core hallmarks of biallelic LoF cases (reported as characteristic in 26/26 LoF cases analyzed by Iruzubieta et al.), the claim that seizures independently exceed 75% penetrance remains conflicted and lacks definitive pooled confirmation.

evidence.text: A systematic analysis of 50 patients with biallelic NOTCH3 variants identified 26 patients with biallelic loss-of-function variants, who presented with a severe neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by spasticity, childhood-onset stroke, and periatrial white matter volume loss.

source.title: Clinical and neuroradiological spectrum of biallelic variants in NOTCH3
source.quote: Biallelic loss-of-function variants (26 patients) lead to a neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by spasticity, childhood-onset stroke, and periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia.

evidence.text: Two siblings with homozygous nonsense null variants (p.Arg735Ter) presented with severe congenital phenotypes including epilepsy, global developmental delay, and pyramidal tract signs.

evidence.text: A patient with a homozygous null frameshift variant (c.2984delC) in NOTCH3 presented with seizures, ataxia, and livedo racemosa, confirming seizures as a recognized manifestation.

source.title: Distinct neurological phenotypes associated with biallelic loss of NOTCH3 function: evidence for recessive inheritance
source.quote: Whole exome sequencing (WES) was performed on a proband who exhibited livedo racemosa, ataxia, cognitive decline, seizures, and MRI white matter abnormalities without anterior temporal pole lesions.

conflicts: While spasticity and seizures are repeatedly reported in biallelic NOTCH3 loss-of-function probands, some patients with early-onset biallelic NOTCH3 disease present without spasticity, and seizures are characterized as variable rather than universal or strictly penetrant at >75%.

Systematic pooled cohorts differentiate biallelic null/loss-of-function variants (predominantly childhood-onset neurodevelopmental disorder with spasticity and stroke) from biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (CADASIL spectrum), but do not yet establish a confirmed epidemiological seizure frequency exceeding 75% across all pediatric null cases.

new_directions.question_text: What is the pooled prevalence and electroclinical classification of epilepsy specifically in patients harboring biallelic null/frameshift/nonsense variants versus cysteine-sparing missense variants?
new_directions.rationale: Determining exact seizure frequencies and EEG characteristics across all documented biallelic NOTCH3 LoF cases will clarify whether epilepsy meets standard diagnostic criterion thresholds (>75%).

new_directions.question_text: Do anterior temporal pole sparing and periatrial leukomalacia reliably distinguish biallelic loss-of-function NOTCH3 cases from early-onset atypical CADASIL on neuroimaging?
new_directions.rationale: Neuroimaging patterns (such as anterior temporal pole sparing and periventricular volume loss) are recurrently noted in recessive null cases and may offer higher diagnostic discrimination than clinical seizures alone.
